name: Ouroboros Field Adjuster's Weathershell Coat
description:
Ouroboros field adjusters spend their working hours in places that corporate offices are not — accident sites, contested claim zones, post-incident industrial floors, and occasionally the outer Shelf where clients in arrears need to be located. Their uniform coat reflects this. The outer shell is a deep charcoal weatherproof membrane bonded to a thermal mid-layer, rated for Meridian 88's lake-effect winters and the ambient chemical mist that drifts in from the refinery districts. The Ouroboros serpent-circle is embossed on the left chest in a self-healing polymer print that resists abrasion and fading. Breast and inner pockets are reinforced with RFID-shielded lining to protect the claim tablets and biometric scanners adjusters carry in the field.

The coat is designed to be professional enough to enter a Tier 3 business lobby and durable enough to walk a flood-damaged Tier 1 basement without destroying itself. Adjusters describe this as the coat's defining tension — it must look like it belongs in a boardroom and survive a demolition site. Most field adjusters develop a specific relationship with their coat over the years, treating it as a work tool rather than clothing. The coat is replaced on a three-year cycle by Ouroboros, and many adjusters negotiate to keep their old ones as a condition of renewal.
cultural_context: An Ouroboros field adjuster arriving at a claim site is a complicated presence. They represent money — the possibility of a payout — and also the machinery that decides whether that payout happens. In Tier 1 and 2 communities, the coat is recognized and produces a specific social calculation: cooperate, or don't. Adjusters who work the Shelf long enough learn to read that calculation quickly.
story_hooks: A player encounters a dead field adjuster in a Shelf building collapse — their claim tablet is locked but still transmitting.
An adjuster arrives to assess a claim that, if paid out, would destabilize a local Shelf community's relationship with a corponation.
Someone is impersonating an Ouroboros adjuster to gain access to post-incident sites before legitimate investigators arrive.
